issues.legal_issue: A dedication of property to a deity may constitute a transfer by gift when the substance of the transaction conveys the property for religious purposes.
material_facts: An intermediary executed a document setting apart part of an estate exclusively for the religious and charitable purposes previously supported by a charge on the estate.
The intermediary appointed himself trustee of the property set apart for those purposes.
issues.conclusion: The dedication was a transfer by gift within the meaning of the Act.
issues.legal_principle: The substance of a transaction dedicating property to a deity determines whether it is a transfer; such a dedication can be a gift. The Court approved Champa Bibi v. Panchiram Nahata, AIR 1963 Cal. 551, which treated a dedication to a Hindu deity as a transfer by gift under section 5A(7) of the West Bengal Estates Acquisition Act, 1953.

predicates.transfer_review_proceeding: A proceeding reviews whether an intermediary's transaction transferring land is legally a transfer.
predicates.property_dedicated_to_deity: The intermediary dedicated property to a deity.
predicates.dedication_conveys_property_for_religiou: The substance of the transaction set property apart for religious purposes.

issues.definition: When a proceeding reviews a land transaction and the substance of the transaction conveys property to a deity for religious purposes, the dedication is treated as a transfer by gift.

issues.legal_issue: A finding that a transfer was not bona fide must be supported by consideration of whether it was made to increase the transferor’s retained land or compensation, and cannot rest merely on transfers to family members.
material_facts: The intermediary dedicated land absolutely to a deity, although the land produced more income than the intermediary's share of the expenditure secured by the earlier charge.

The Settlement Officer relied on transfers of the remaining property to the intermediary's son and wife and repeated the statutory criteria, but did not explain how the challenged transaction would increase the land the intermediary could retain or the compensation payable.
The appellate authority did not examine whether the transaction served either of those objectives, and the High Court did not address that question.
issues.conclusion: The authorities below erred in finding the transfer not bona fide without assessing whether it was made to increase the amount of land the intermediary could retain or the compensation payable; the matter required fresh consideration.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 5A(7) of the West Bengal Estates Acquisition Act, 1953, a transfer is not bona fide if made principally or partially to increase the land a person may retain or the compensation payable. A transfer to a son or wife, by itself, does not establish lack of bona fides. The decision-maker must give reasons connecting the transaction to one of the statutory objectives.

predicates.challenge_to_adverse_transfer_finding: A proceeding challenges an adverse finding that a land transfer was not bona fide.
predicates.decisionmaker_failed_to_assess_retention: The decision-maker did not assess whether the transfer was made to increase the transferor's retained land or compensation.

issues.definition: When an adverse finding about a transfer is challenged and the decision-maker did not assess whether the transfer pursued either specified advantage, the finding requires reconsideration based on the transfer's purpose.

issues.legal_issue: A pre-existing religious charge and the documents establishing it did not raise a claim to retain land under the statutory provision for land held under a qualifying trust or endowment.
material_facts: A prior decree had recognized a charge on the estate for religious and charitable purposes.
The claim concerned the position before the later challenged document and under the unamended Act.
issues.conclusion: No question under section 6(1)(i) arose on these facts; the prior decree and instrument did not bring the land within that provision.
issues.legal_principle: Section 6(1)(i) concerns specified land held for an exclusive religious or charitable purpose under a trust, endowment or legal obligation. Following Fazlul Rabbi Pradhan v. State of West Bengal, [1965] 3 SCR 307, the Court held that the earlier decree and instrument did not bring the land within this provision; the question had to be considered in the situation existing before the challenged document and under the unamended Act.

predicates.retention_claim_proceeding: A proceeding concerns whether land may be retained under a category for religious or charitable purposes.
predicates.claim_based_on_preexisting_religious_cha: The asserted basis for retaining the land is a charge on the property for religious or charitable purposes.
predicates.prior_decree_or_instrument_only_reiterat: An earlier decree or instrument merely recognized or reiterated the charge rather than establishing that the land was held under a qualifying trust or endowment.

issues.definition: When a retention claim rests on a pre-existing religious charge that an earlier decree or instrument merely recognized or reiterated, that charge alone does not establish qualifying retention.
